tools.name: search_guidelines
tools.description:
Look a rule up in the UMR guidelines (umr4nlp/umr-guidelines, guidelines.md).

keywords: terms to look for, e.g. "aspect", "modal strength", "have-rel-role-92", ":quant",
"reentrancy". Passages with more of the keywords come first, then those whose heading has
them, then those that mention them most.
max_results: how many passages to return (at most 10).

Returns {"sections": [{"heading": the passage's place in the guidelines ("Part 3. ... > Part
3-3-1. Aspect"), "text": the passage (a section, or a part of a long one)}], "found": how
many passages matched}.

tools.name: propbank_lookup
tools.description:
Look up a lemma and every alternate of it in PropBank (at most 20 per call).

language is "en" or "zh". Returns Markdown: per lemma, every roleset with its roles and all
its examples (the sentence, then each argument; traces such as *T*-1 are PropBank's own),
or "not in PropBank". Lemmas over the limit are not looked up: the last line names them
(call again with them). There is no PropBank for another language (Uzbek): nothing.

tools.name: search_annotations
tools.description:
Find how a case is annotated: gold UMR annotations of whole sentences.

language: "zh" (Chinese) or "en" (English).
keywords: words or pieces to look for, matched anywhere in a sentence or its annotation:
words of the text (e.g. "发生", "wanted to"), concepts ("have-org-role-91", "identity-91"),
roles (":ARG1-of", ":manner"), attribute values (":aspect state"). Sentences with more of the
keywords come first.
max_results: how many gold sentences to return (at most 10).

Returns {"gold": [{"doc", "sentence_number", "sentence", "annotation"}], where annotation is
the sentence's whole annotation (words, sentence-level graph, alignment, document-level
annotation); "found": how many gold sentences matched in all}.

messages.content:
## Input

Language: en
Document: en-0008, sentence 9 of 9

The previous sentences (at most five; number, tab, words):

4	Russian President Vladimir Putin pardoned him for health reasons .

5	Pope was flown to the U.S. military base at Ramstein , Germany .

6	He will spend the next several days at the medical center there before he returns home with his wife Sherry .

7	Pope was in remission from a rare form of bone cancer when he was arrested in Russia.

8	Doctors will examine him for signs that the cancer may have come back while he [was] awaiting trial in a Russian jail.

Their graphs:

I checked `pardon` in PropBank and used `pardon-01` ("legally relieve of guilt"): Putin is the ARG0 (the one who pardons) and "him" is the ARG1 (the person pardoned). The gold data had nothing on this sentence or a similar pardon, so the rest follows the guidelines.

- **Putin's title:** "Russian President" uses `have-org-role-92`, with Russia as `:ARG2` and `president` as `:ARG3`.
- **"Him":** this is a 3rd-person singular `person`. Linking it to the person named earlier (probably Edmund Pope) happens at the document level, not here.
- **"For health reasons":** I wrote this as `:cause (reason :mod health)`, with a node for "reasons". One gold sentence ("for moral reasons") uses `:ARG1-of cause-01` with `reason` as `:ARG0` instead, so the gold may differ here.
- **Aspect:** `performance`, because the pardon is a completed past event.

# ::snt 4
# sentence level graph:
(s4p / pardon-01
    :ARG0 (s4p2 / person
        :wiki "Vladimir_Putin"
        :name (s4n / name :op1 "Vladimir" :op2 "Putin")
        :ARG1-of (s4h / have-org-role-92
            :ARG2 (s4c / country
                :wiki "Russia"
                :name (s4n2 / name :op1 "Russia"))
            :ARG3 (s4p3 / president)))
    :ARG1 (s4p4 / person
        :refer-person 3rd
        :refer-number singular)
    :cause (s4r / reason
        :mod (s4h2 / health))
    :aspect performance)

I used fly-01, whose ARG1 is the passenger. Pope is that passenger, and nobody is named as the one who flew him. The node's alignment and the document-level links will be added in the later step.

# ::snt 5
# sentence level graph:
(s5f / fly-01
    :ARG1 (s5p / person
        :name (s5n / name :op1 "Pope"))
    :goal (s5b / base
        :mod (s5m / military)
        :mod (s5c / country
            :wiki "United_States"
            :name (s5n2 / name :op1 "U.S."))
        :place (s5c2 / city
            :wiki "Ramstein-Miesenbach"
            :name (s5n3 / name :op1 "Ramstein")
            :part-of (s5c3 / country
                :wiki "Germany"
                :name (s5n4 / name :op1 "Germany"))))
    :aspect performance)

A few choices in the graph:
- **Destination:** "to the U.S. military base" is `:goal`, following the PropBank example "fly to San Francisco".
- **Pope:** a `person` with the name "Pope". I took the name from the sentence alone; I couldn't see the earlier sentences.
- **Aspect:** `performance`, because the flight is finished and reached its destination.
- **The base:** "military" and "U.S." are both `:mod` on `base`. Ramstein is a `city` placed on the base with `:place`, and it is `:part-of` Germany. No gold example for "military base" or "Ramstein" came up, so the structure of this phrase is my own judgment.
- **Wiki title for Ramstein:** I used "Ramstein-Miesenbach" for the town. "Ramstein_Air_Base" would also be a reasonable choice.

# ::snt 6
# sentence level graph:
(s6s / spend-02
    :ARG0 (s6p / person
        :refer-person 3rd
        :refer-number singular)
    :ARG1 (s6d / day
        :quant (s6s2 / several)
        :mod (s6n / next))
    :place (s6c / center
        :mod (s6m / medical)
        :place (s6t / there))
    :temporal (s6b / before
        :op1 (s6r / return-01
            :ARG1 s6p
            :ARG4 (s6h / home)
            :companion (s6p2 / person
                :name (s6n2 / name :op1 "Sherry")
                :ARG1-of (s6h2 / have-rel-role-92
                    :ARG2 s6p
                    :ARG3 (s6w / wife)
                    :aspect state))
            :aspect performance))
    :aspect performance)

# ::snt 7
# sentence level graph:
(s7r / remission-02
    :ARG1 (s7d / disease :wiki "Bone_tumor"
        :name (s7n / name :op1 "bone" :op2 "cancer")
        :mod (s7f / form)
        :mod (s7r2 / rare)
        :possessor (s7p / person :wiki "Edmond_Pope"
            :name (s7n2 / name :op1 "Pope")))
    :temporal (s7a / arrest-01
        :ARG1 s7p
        :place (s7c / country :wiki "Russia"
            :name (s7n3 / name :op1 "Russia"))
        :aspect performance)
    :aspect state)

I had no gold example of "in remission" to copy, so a few choices here are judgement calls:

- **Concept and roles:** I used PropBank `remission-02` ("abate in intensity"). Its `:ARG1` is the thing that abates, so the cancer is `:ARG1` and Pope is linked as its `:possessor`. Another reading would make Pope the `:ARG1` and attach the cancer with `:source`.
- **"a rare form of bone cancer":** In a gold example, "a form of asbestos" is annotated as `asbestos :mod (form)`. I did the same here, and added `rare` as a second `:mod`.
- **The disease:** I wrote "bone cancer" as a named `disease`, the way gold examples treat "cancer". The wiki title "Bone_tumor" is my guess.
- **Pope:** He is "Pope" here, a person probably named in full in an earlier sentence. The wiki value "Edmond_Pope" is my assumption.
- **The "when" clause:** The arrest is the remission's `:temporal`, with performance aspect (a completed past event). The remission is a state.

# ::snt 8
# sentence level graph:
(s8e / examine-01
    :ARG0 (s8d / doctor
        :refer-number plural)
    :ARG1 (s8p / person
        :refer-person 3rd
        :refer-number singular)
    :ARG2 (s8s / signal-07
        :ARG1 (s8r / return-01
            :ARG1 (s8c / cancer)
            :temporal (s8a / await-01
                :ARG1 s8p
                :ARG2 (s8t / try-02
                    :ARG1 s8p
                    :aspect process)
                :place (s8j / jail
                    :mod (s8c2 / country
                        :wiki "Russia"
                        :name (s8n / name :op1 "Russia")))
                :aspect activity)
            :modal-strength neutral-affirmative
            :aspect performance)
        :aspect state)
    :aspect performance)

My choices:
- **examine-01:** The doctors are its `:ARG0`, "him" is its `:ARG1`, and the "signs" go in `:ARG2` because PropBank defines that role as "in search of what". The examining has not happened yet ("will"), but it is a single event that is meant to be completed, so its aspect is `performance`.
- **signs → signal-07:** PropBank has no rolesets for "sign" or "come back" as a phrasal verb. I used `signal-07` here; its `:ARG1` is the thing shown, which is the cancer coming back. I chose aspect `state` for it.
- **come back → return-01:** Since "come back" has no roleset of its own, I used `return-01` ("come back"), with the cancer as its `:ARG1`. Because of "may", it is marked `:modal-strength neutral-affirmative`.
- **while he was awaiting trial → await-01:** This is a `:temporal` modifier of the return. In `await-01` the person waiting is `:ARG1`, the trial (`try-02`, aspect `process`) is `:ARG2`, and the waiting is ongoing, so its aspect is `activity`.
- **Russian jail:** The jail has `:place`, and "Russian" is a `:mod` holding the named country Russia.
- **Same person three times:** "him", the person waiting and the person on trial are all one node (`s8p`), used again in each place.

I could not find gold examples of this construction to compare against. The least certain choices are `signal-07` for "signs" and its `state` aspect.

This sentence:

9	A spokeswoman said that Pope was suffering from malnutrition and high blood pressure .

Its graph:

# ::snt 9
# sentence level graph:
(s9s / say-01
    :ARG0 (s9p / person
        :ARG1-of (s9h / have-org-role-92
            :ARG3 (s9s2 / spokeswoman)))
    :ARG1 (s9s3 / suffer-01
        :ARG0 (s9p2 / person
            :name (s9n / name :op1 "Pope"))
        :ARG1 (s9a / and
            :op1 (s9m / malnutrition)
            :op2 (s9p3 / pressure
                :mod (s9b / blood)
                :ARG1-of (s9h2 / high-02
                    :aspect state)))
        :aspect state)
    :aspect performance)

My notes on the choices:
- **Spokeswoman:** I followed two gold examples, which show "spokeswoman" as a `person` with `have-org-role-92`. This sentence names no organization, so the role has no `:ARG2`.
- **Pope:** I treated "Pope" as the person's name. Earlier sentences probably give the full name (likely Edmund Pope), but only "Pope" appears here, so the name has one `:op`.
- **Senses:** PropBank confirms `say-01` (the spokeswoman is `:ARG0`, what she said is `:ARG1`) and `suffer-01` (Pope is `:ARG0`, the illnesses are `:ARG1`).
- **"High blood pressure":** this is `pressure`, with `blood` as `:mod` and `high-02` as `:ARG1-of`. I didn't look up `high-02` in PropBank, so that sense is unchecked.
- **Aspect of "was suffering":** this was a close call. I chose `state` because suffering from an illness is a condition, not a process. Since the verb is in the progressive, the gold annotation may use `activity` instead.
- **No `:quote`:** this is indirect speech, not a quotation, so I left it out.

content.text:
# document level relations:
(d / document
    :temporal ((document-creation-time :before s9s)
               (s9s :overlap s9s3))
    :modal ((root :modal author)
            (author :full-affirmative s9s)
            (author :full-affirmative s9p)
            (s9p :full-affirmative s9s3))
    :coref ((s8p :same-entity s9p2)))

I worked from the abridged guidelines only and did not call any tools.

- **Temporal:** The spokeswoman's saying (`s9s`) is a past event, so it comes before the time the document was written. The suffering (`s9s3`) is in the clause she reports, so it takes the saying as its reference time. I marked them as overlapping because "was suffering" describes his condition at the time she spoke.
- **Modal:** The author asserts that the spokeswoman spoke. The spokeswoman (`s9p`) is the one who is sure that Pope was suffering. This follows the guidelines' rule for reported speech.
- **Coreference:** "Pope" here (`s9p2`) is the same person as "him" in sentence 8 (`s8p`), his closest earlier mention.
- **Left out:** I gave no temporal relation to `high-02` (`s9h2`) or to the spokeswoman's role node (`s9h`). If the gold version orders every state, it may add `(s9s3 :overlap s9h2)`, and I would lose that one relation.
